situations.name: Tauri IPC call wrappers
situations.definition: A developer needs to call a Rust backend command from the frontend and wants the canonical wrapper (timeout, arg coercion, dedup, auth token, metrics).
situations.note: Enforced by ESLint no-restricted-imports and near-universal, but the wrapper carries a documented at-least-once hazard (timeout does not cancel the backend) that every mutating caller must reason about; App.tsx still bypasses it once with a raw invoke.

situations.name: Backend event subscription
situations.definition: A developer needs to receive a Rust-emitted Tauri event in React (or in a store) with correct typing, teardown, and no duplicate listeners.
situations.note: Four overlapping answers exist (typedListen, useTauriEvent, createSingletonListener, the central eventBridge registry) and 63 files still import @tauri-apps/api/event directly; choosing wrong yields duplicate subscriptions or events dropped before mount.

situations.name: Zustand domain slices
situations.definition: A developer is adding new client state and must decide where it lives, how it composes into a domain store, and what its loading/error shape is.
situations.note: The slice pattern and createCoreState() are followed consistently, but the boundary between a slice on a domain store and a standalone micro-store (toast, i18n, commandPalette, auth, notificationCenter) is undocumented and decided case by case.

situations.name: Cross-store communication
situations.definition: A developer needs one domain store to react to, or read from, another without importing it directly.
situations.note: Central wiring file makes the graph visible, but every new event costs an entry in three places (event map, wiring, subscriber) so the temptation to just call useXStore.getState() persists.

situations.name: Client state persistence
situations.definition: A developer needs a piece of UI state to survive app restart and must choose between zustand persist, the backend app_settings mirror, and raw localStorage.
situations.note: Only 5 stores use persist and 9 files use the deduped/throttled storage helpers, yet 430 raw localStorage references exist; localStorage is per-webview-profile so unmirrored state silently vanishes on profile reset — the exact loss appearanceMirror was built to fix, applied to only one key.

situations.name: Stale response guards
situations.definition: A developer fires an async fetch whose result may land after a newer one and needs the newer write to win.
situations.note: The helper's own docstring says several slices independently reimplemented the counter/compare pattern; only 9 files adopted it, so most fetch paths still race on StrictMode double-mount and rapid filter changes.

situations.name: Cached and deduped fetching
situations.definition: A developer wants repeated reads of the same backend data to not re-hit IPC on every mount or filter change.
situations.note: Five separate caching answers coexist (three lib helpers, module-scoped view caches per the loading doctrine, and an implicit 250ms auto-dedup inside invokeWithTimeout); nothing says which layer owns caching, so callers stack them.

situations.name: Error resolution and display
situations.definition: A developer catches a raw backend/JS error and must turn it into something a user can act on.
situations.note: Five layers (errorRegistry rules, errorPipeline classification, errorTaxonomy, ApiError severity, the translated bridge) plus four banner components; only 18 files call resolveError, so most surfaces render the raw string.

situations.name: Swallowed error telemetry
situations.definition: A developer has a background promise that can fail and needs the failure logged/breadcrumbed rather than silently dropped.
situations.note: Strongest convergence in the slice (1271 silentCatch + 604 toastCatch, backed by two ESLint rules); the remaining judgement call is silent vs toast, which is not encoded anywhere.

situations.name: Toasts and transient feedback
situations.definition: A developer needs to tell the user that something just succeeded or failed, without blocking them.
situations.note: One store with priority-aware eviction and ARIA announcement; the sharp edge is that a toast type also implies a duration, an ARIA politeness and an eviction priority that callers rarely think about.

situations.name: OS notifications
situations.definition: A developer wants to notify the user outside the app window when a long-running process finishes.
situations.note: Two full implementations with different permission models — the Tauri plugin-notification path and a Web Notification API path that claims 'no plugin required'; nothing says which wins.

situations.name: Attention counts and badges
situations.definition: A developer adds a domain whose 'items needing action' count must show up on the sidebar, a tab, or a dashboard header.
situations.note: Built specifically to end sidebar-vs-dashboard count drift, but the notification center keeps its own store and the registry only covers five domains.

situations.name: Error boundaries
situations.definition: A developer needs a render crash to degrade gracefully rather than blank the app, and must pick a boundary flavour.
situations.note: Three distinct boundaries with different fallbacks (shared ErrorBoundary, App's SilentErrorBoundary with backoff retry, main.tsx's untranslated Sentry root fallback); placement is ad hoc — the global overlays share one boundary as an acknowledged stopgap.

situations.name: Route and chunk splitting
situations.definition: A developer makes a route/overlay lazy and must handle chunk-load failure, the loading gap, and prefetch warming.
situations.note: 104 raw React.lazy call sites vs 9 using lazyRetry; a raw lazy caches a rejected chunk fetch forever (a known incident in this repo), and only 11 files use the canonical delayed Suspense fallback.

situations.name: Deferred and idle work
situations.definition: A developer has non-critical startup work (prefetch, seed, cleanup) that must not compete with first paint.
situations.note: Three mechanisms — idlePrefetch, DeferUntilIdle, and hand-rolled requestIdleCallback-with-setTimeout-fallback ladders in App.tsx — plus magic delays (2000ms, 4000ms) with no shared budget.

situations.name: Periodic refresh and polling
situations.definition: A developer needs a surface to re-fetch on a cadence without spawning yet another desynchronised timer.
situations.note: The coordinator exists precisely because 7+ surfaces each spun their own interval, yet only 14 files use usePolling against 121 raw setInterval references; the bypass path loses visibility-pause and backoff.

situations.name: Buttons and click actions
situations.definition: A developer needs a clickable control with the app's variants, sizes, disabled/busy state and focus ring.
situations.note: Worst raw-vs-primitive ratio in the slice: 1119 of 2104 tsx files contain a raw <button> while only 58 import the canonical Button and 40 AsyncButton; every hand-roll re-decides padding, radius, focus ring, and disabled opacity.

situations.name: Dropdowns and selects
situations.definition: A developer needs the user to pick one value from a list.
situations.note: Three primitives with overlapping scope (Listbox 13 files, ThemedSelect 48, ColumnDropdownFilter) plus 49 files still using a raw <select>; CLAUDE.md names Listbox as canonical but ThemedSelect is 4x more adopted.

situations.name: Anchored popovers
situations.definition: A developer needs a menu/popover positioned against a trigger, escaping parent overflow and stacking contexts.
situations.note: Only 3 files use the flip-aware positioning hook while 28 use createPortal and 29 measure with getBoundingClientRect directly; viewport-clamping and flip behaviour are re-derived per popover.

situations.name: Click-outside dismissal
situations.definition: A developer needs an open menu/panel/popover to close when the user clicks elsewhere or presses Escape.
situations.note: 11 files use the hook, 46 attach their own mousedown/pointerdown listeners; portal-rendered children make the containment check subtle and hand-rolls routinely get it wrong.

situations.name: Form fields and validation
situations.definition: A developer builds an input with a label, hint, error message, and validation timing.
situations.note: The most sophisticated primitive in the slice (validation timing modes, async availability, error registry feeding a summary banner) with only 4 adopters, against 289 files containing a raw <input>; the whole form-error architecture is effectively unused.

situations.name: Confirming destructive actions
situations.definition: A developer must make the user confirm before something irreversible happens.
situations.note: Three near-identical confirmation shells (24 / 6 / 4 adopters) differing mainly in whether they require typing a name; nothing states which risk class demands which.

situations.name: Empty states
situations.definition: A developer must render a data region that legitimately has nothing in it, ideally with a next action.
situations.note: CLAUDE.md and the reuse doc both point at feedback/EmptyState — WHICH DOES NOT EXIST. Fifteen separate *EmptyState components live across features; the two real shared ones (ScenarioEmptyState, IllustratedEmptyState) are variant-enumerating and cannot absorb new cases without an edit.

situations.name: Busy and loading indicators
situations.definition: A developer needs to show that an inline action or region is working.
situations.note: The named canonical primitive was deliberately neutered to render nothing ('spinners are intentionally disabled app-wide') while 184 files — including the shared Button, AsyncButton and FormField themselves — hand-roll animate-spin. The doctrine and the code contradict each other.

situations.name: Page loading choreography
situations.definition: A developer builds a data surface and must sequence chrome, skeleton, and row reveal without flashing.
situations.note: Already documented elsewhere (loading pattern v2, five laws) — listed for recurrence only.

situations.name: Data tables
situations.definition: A developer needs a sortable, filterable table with loading and empty behaviour.
situations.note: Already documented elsewhere — listed for recurrence only (UnifiedTable 25, DataGrid 16).

situations.name: Modal and dialog shells
situations.definition: A developer needs an overlay panel with backdrop, focus trap, escape handling, and stacking.
situations.note: Already documented elsewhere; enforced by custom/enforce-base-modal. Residual signal: 46 files still contain a raw `fixed inset-0` backdrop.

situations.name: Tooltips and hover help
situations.definition: A developer needs to attach explanatory text to a control or truncated value.
situations.note: Good adoption (120 files) but 74 files still use a bare title= attribute, and TruncateWithTooltip — the answer for the most common case — has 2 adopters.

situations.name: Timestamp display
situations.definition: A developer needs to render 'when' something happened in a locale-correct, live-updating way.
situations.note: Component path (RelativeTime/AbsoluteTime, shared ticker) and string path (formatters.timeAgo/formatTimestamp) both live, and the string path is not reactive or localized.

situations.name: Number and duration formatting
situations.definition: A developer needs to render a count, percentage, cost, or elapsed time consistently.
situations.note: Numeric (110 files) plus a large formatters module plus AnimatedCounter/SpringCount, against 129 files calling toFixed/toLocaleString directly; there is an ESLint rule (custom/prefer-numeric) but it only warns.

situations.name: Backend status tokens
situations.definition: A developer receives a machine token from Rust ('queued', 'critical') and must render it as a localized label with the right colour.
situations.note: Two half-answers must be combined by hand: tokenLabel for the text (32 adopters) and statusTokens/STATUS_PALETTE for the colour, with a legacy EXECUTION_STATUS_MAP in formatters still carrying its own colour table.

situations.name: i18n string authoring
situations.definition: A developer adds a user-facing string and must place it in the right locale section, route-declare it, and translate it everywhere.
situations.note: Excellent adoption (1450 components) but three access paths (useTranslation, getActiveTranslations, the module-scope `en` proxy in 56 files) and a silent failure mode: a section not listed in routeSections.ts renders English forever in every locale with no signal.

situations.name: Design token usage
situations.definition: A developer styles a new surface and must pick spacing, radius, shadow, and type from the token system rather than raw Tailwind.
situations.note: Seven custom ESLint rules police it (no-raw-spacing/radius/shadow/text-classes, no-direct-white-colors, low-contrast) and the repo carries ~10k warnings; tokens are split between a JS module, Tailwind semantic classes, and a 5.5k-line CSS file with no single index.

situations.name: Theming and appearance
situations.definition: A developer adds a surface that must look right in 12 themes plus custom, at three brightness levels, three densities, and three text scales.
situations.note: Four independent axes (theme id, brightness multiplier, density, text scale) plus a per-persona 'vibe' override layer and a runtime-injected custom-theme stylesheet; only 19 files reference [data-theme] and useDensity has 2 adopters, so most components silently assume the default.

situations.name: Motion and reduced motion
situations.definition: A developer animates something and must respect the reduced-motion preference and the app's timing vocabulary.
situations.note: 215 files import framer-motion directly against 57 using useMotion; three preset vocabularies exist (animationPresets MOTION_PRESETS, designTokens MOTION, display/motionPresets) and a custom ESLint rule exists only because the fallback is so often forgotten.

situations.name: List entrance reveal
situations.definition: A developer wants rows/tiles to appear with a stagger the first time they arrive, without re-animating on every update.
situations.note: Strong convergence on RevealItem + useProgressiveReveal, but AnimatedList and Reveal are near-duplicate answers with 6 and 1 adopters.

situations.name: Keyboard shortcut registration
situations.definition: A developer wires a global key binding and must place it correctly relative to modals, palette, and nav mode.
situations.note: One provider with a documented priority ladder (0-100) and a registry that drives the cheat sheet — genuinely canonical. The hard part is that priority numbers are a global resource with no allocation rule, and forgetting the registry entry silently un-documents the binding.

situations.name: Command palette entries
situations.definition: A developer wants a new destination, action, or setting to be reachable from Cmd+K.
situations.note: Navigation entries derive from the nav registry so they cannot drift, but non-nav item kinds (agent-action, setting, action) are assembled inline in a 473-line component with no registration seam.

situations.name: Navigation destinations
situations.definition: A developer adds a new top-level surface and must make it reachable, gated, tracked, and back-button-aware in a URL-less app.
situations.note: Exemplary consolidation — four catalogs collapsed into one registry with a compile-time exhaustiveness assertion and a completeness test. The remaining difficulty is that routing state lives in a persisted store, so 'the route' is also a rehydration concern.

situations.name: Screen-reader announcements
situations.definition: A developer needs a non-focus state change (saved, loaded, error) to be spoken by assistive tech.
situations.note: The provider solves a real hard problem (queued flush so a burst of announcements is not collapsed into one utterance) but has 3 callers, while 64 files hand-roll their own aria-live region — each of which has the collapse bug the provider exists to fix.

situations.name: Focus management
situations.definition: A developer opens/closes a surface and must move, trap, restore, or roam focus correctly.
situations.note: BaseModal owns the trap for modals; everything else is ad hoc across 65 files calling .focus() directly, and useRovingTabIndex — the primitive for list/grid keyboard roaming — has ZERO adopters.

situations.name: Copy to clipboard
situations.definition: A developer needs a value copyable with confirmation feedback.
situations.note: Cleanest convergence in the slice — 67 adopters, only 4 raw clipboard.writeText calls, backed by an ESLint rule (custom/prefer-shared-clipboard).

situations.name: Long-list virtualization
situations.definition: A developer renders a list that can grow to thousands of rows without dropping frames.
situations.note: No external virtualization library; three in-house answers (the hook, GroupedVirtualList with sticky headers, UnifiedTable's own path) and the decision of when a list needs virtualizing is undocumented.

situations.name: Drag and drop
situations.definition: A developer needs items reorderable or a target that accepts a dropped file.
situations.note: @dnd-kit is a dependency, KanbanBoard uses raw HTML5 DnD, and DragHandle/DropIndicator/DropZoneGlow are visual-only fragments with 2-3 adopters each; 32 files declare draggable elements with no shared behaviour layer.

situations.name: Chart rendering
situations.definition: A developer needs a chart that does not drag recharts into the initial bundle and matches the app's palette.
situations.note: Total convergence — zero direct recharts imports anywhere; the render-prop shape exists specifically because recharts inspects child identity. Chart gradients are a separate app-root singleton.

situations.name: Markdown and rich output
situations.definition: A developer renders model- or user-authored text that may contain markup.
situations.note: 51 adopters and only 5 dangerouslySetInnerHTML sites, all sanitizer-backed; risk is that this is the main render path for untrusted LLM output.

situations.name: Streaming CLI output
situations.definition: A developer needs to display live process/agent stdout with ANSI colour, search, and classification.
situations.note: Two TerminalBody components exist (shared/components/terminal and shared/components/progress) and xterm is a separate path used by Fleet; the choice between 'render lines' and 'run a real terminal' is not documented.

situations.name: Untrusted input sanitization
situations.definition: A developer handles content from an LLM, an external API, or an imported bundle and must neutralize it before use.
situations.note: Nine sanitizers with no index or policy saying which boundary requires which; maskSensitive has 2 adopters despite the app being a credential vault, and SurfaceSpec adds a separate 'injection-free by construction' model for agent-emitted UI.

situations.name: Agent-declared UI
situations.definition: A developer wants a persona run to emit interactive UI rather than prose, without letting a model inject arbitrary markup.
situations.note: Low recurrence, very high consequence: a zod grammar whose node set IS the blessed catalog, with a salvage pass that drops bad blocks instead of failing, and a hard rule that actions never auto-run.

situations.name: Structured logging
situations.definition: A developer needs a diagnostic line that will be useful in a shipped build.
situations.note: 100 files use createLogger against 93 raw console.* calls; the logger's own docstring admits it only writes to console and never forwards to the Rust backend, so prod logs are effectively lost.

situations.name: Usage analytics
situations.definition: A developer wants a feature's usage, activation milestone, or conversion tracked without leaking user content.
situations.note: Clean pluggable-sink seam gated on a telemetry preference; the sink is still Sentry-only and the privacy contract ('identifier strings only') is enforced by convention, not by types.

situations.name: App settings read/write
situations.definition: A developer needs a durable, backend-stored preference readable from any panel.
situations.note: Solid: microtask-coalesced bulk reads plus a backend 'settings-changed' event so panels stay live. Overlaps confusingly with theme/appearance state, which chose localStorage-plus-mirror instead.

situations.name: Tier and capability gating
situations.definition: A developer must hide or disable a surface for users below a tier, or in non-dev builds.
situations.note: Three mechanisms — nav registry gates, useTier at render, and raw import.meta.env.DEV branches. App.tsx documents a shipped bug caused by fusing a dev gate to a non-dev feature; the same trap is reachable from any DEV branch.

situations.name: Per-action async state
situations.definition: A developer triggers a store action from a button and needs that specific action's loading/error state, not the store's global flag.
situations.note: 331 reportError calls write into the scoped sliceErrors map, but useSliceError has 1 reader and useAsyncAction has 1 — meaning almost all recorded per-action errors are never rendered anywhere.

situations.name: Debounced autosave
situations.definition: A developer edits a field that should persist without an explicit Save press, and show that it saved.
situations.note: Five overlapping answers with 1-5 adopters each (debounced save, save feedback flag, settings save toast, a checkmark animation, and useAppSetting's own `saved` flag); no rule says which combination is the pattern.

situations.name: Unsaved-changes guards
situations.definition: A developer must stop a user from navigating away from a dirty editor.
situations.note: Hook and modal are paired 1:1 across 4 surfaces, but the app has no URL router — the guard must intercept store-driven navigation, so any new nav entry point can bypass it silently.

situations.name: Page and section scaffolding
situations.definition: A developer starts a new page or panel and needs the standard header, padding, card, and action-row structure.
situations.note: ContentLayout (81) and SectionCard (37) are well adopted, but SectionHeader/SectionHeading/SectionLabel/ActionRow overlap heavily and there is no stated composition order; a PanelShell extraction is already on the reuse backlog.

situations.name: Tab strips and view switching
situations.definition: A developer needs to switch between sub-views inside a page or panel.
situations.note: SegmentedTabs (22) dominates, PanelTabBar (4) and feature-local tab bars persist; the difference between the two shared ones is visual only and undocumented.

situations.name: Collection filtering and search
situations.definition: A developer gives the user a way to narrow a list by facet, query, or sort.
situations.note: Six partial answers (FilterBar chrome, column dropdown, two collection hooks, a facet-tree model, a match highlighter) that do not compose; each surface reassembles filtering from scratch.

situations.name: Scroll affordances
situations.definition: A developer has a scrollable region and needs edge shadows, position restoration, or infinite-scroll triggering.
situations.note: The hook (10) outdraws its own container component (3), and restoration matters more than usual here because lazy routes fully unmount on nav-away.

situations.name: Persona visual identity
situations.definition: A developer renders an agent's icon, avatar, or sigil from a free-form icon string.
situations.note: resolvePersonaIcon was built to collapse a real two-renderer divergence and includes SSRF sanitization of URL icons; the parallel glyph/sigil system (36 files) is a second, much larger identity surface with no equivalent single resolver.

situations.name: Dispatching work to an agent
situations.definition: A developer builds a surface that hands a prepared prompt to an agent and must get user consent about transport.
situations.note: One consent surface over four transports with very different observability and cost profiles (dev runner, Fleet terminal, headless CLI, OS console the app cannot kill); low recurrence today but every new 'run this' button is a candidate.

situations.name: Decision and approval rows
situations.definition: A developer builds a surface where the user accepts/rejects a stream of proposals.
situations.note: A genuine cross-feature pattern (reviews, backlog, knowledge, triage) with a shared row, action control, faceted table, and a rowWrites write-path used by 19 files.

situations.name: HMR-safe global singletons
situations.definition: A developer has module state (listeners, buffers, coordinators) that must not duplicate across a hot reload.
situations.note: Named in CLAUDE.md as a convention but implemented per-site with hand-written `globalThis.__x ??=` guards and no shared helper or key registry, so two modules can collide on a key.

situations.name: Bounded concurrency fan-out
situations.definition: A developer needs to run the same async call over N items without an unbounded Promise.all.
situations.note: Recently consolidated from two independently-written copies; the docstring explicitly says every fleet-scaled fan-out should route here, but discovery of the helper is the whole problem.

situations.name: Dev-only diagnostics
situations.definition: A developer wants an in-app tool (inspector, freeze watchdog, store monitor, IPC metrics) that must be fully absent from production builds.
situations.note: Consistent import.meta.env.DEV + dynamic-import shape so Rollup drops the branch; the trap is that the same shape applied to a shipping feature silently deletes it (documented incident in App.tsx).

situations.name: Test automation seams
situations.definition: A developer adds UI that must be drivable by the MCP test harness and identifiable by automated tests.
situations.note: 584 files carry data-testid but with no naming convention, and the window.__TEST__ bridge is gated on a DEV-or-env check whose ordering (bridge before perfInstrument) is load-bearing and only documented in a comment.

situations.name: First-use consent and privacy
situations.definition: A developer adds something that phones home or stores data and must respect the consent gate.
situations.note: Consent has a version so a bump re-prompts, and Sentry/analytics init is genuinely gated on it in main.tsx; the risk is that any new telemetry path can simply not consult isTelemetryEnabled().
